Without the dressing it keeps for 1 day: Beetroot and orange salad
3 boiled beetroots
2 oranges
4–5 sprigs mint
If the beetroot is raw, boil it in its skin for 40 minutes, then peel and slice.
Remove the peel and white pith from the oranges and slice.
Slice the onion into thin rings.
Whisk the olive oil, pomegranate molasses and salt.
Arrange on a plate and add the dressing and mint.
Beetroot juice stains your hands; wear gloves.
Bulgur and pomegranate salad
1 pomegranate
4 spring onions
Half a bunch parsley and mint
2 tablespoons pomegranate molasses
1 dessert spoon salt, chilli flakes
Soak the bulgur in hot water and leave covered for 15 minutes to swell.
Seed the pomegranate.
Finely chop the herbs and spring onion.
Work the bulgur with the pomegranate molasses, olive oil, salt and chilli flakes.
Add the herbs and pomegranate seeds and mix.
Add the herbs once the bulgur has cooled so they don’t wilt.
Quinoa avocado salad
1 cup cherry tomatoes
Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve; cook in water for 15 minutes and let cool.
Dice the avocado and cucumber and halve the tomatoes.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon and salt.
Toss the ingredients with the dressing.
Rinsing quinoa removes its bitter taste.
As a main-meal salad.
Without avocado it keeps for 2 days.
Chickpea and cucumber salad
2 cucumbers
1 dessert spoon cumin, salt
Drain the chickpeas.
Dice the cucumber and pepper.
Finely chop the onion.
Make a dressing with olive oil, lemon, cumin and salt.
Toss everything together and let rest for 10 minutes.
Cumin makes chickpeas easier to digest.
Roasted pepper salad with green lentils
3 roasted red peppers
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 teaspoon cumin
Boil the lentils for 20 minutes so they stay firm, and drain.
Peel the roasted peppers and cut into strips.
Chop the herbs.
Whisk the dressing ingredients.
Mix everything and serve.
If you put the peppers in a bag while hot, the skins peel off easily.
Purslane and strawberry salad
Half a cup lor cheese
Remove the thick purslane stems and wash.
Quarter the strawberries.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon, honey and salt.
Toss the purslane and strawberries with the dressing.
Sprinkle the lor and walnuts on top.
Dry the purslane well so the dressing clings.
Buckwheat and tomato salad
Half a bunch mint and parsley
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 teaspoon chilli flakes
Wash the buckwheat and cook in water for 12–15 minutes so it stays firm; drain and let cool.
Dice the tomato and onion small.
Make a dressing with pomegranate molasses, olive oil, salt and chilli flakes.
Overcooked buckwheat turns sticky; keep it firm.
White bean and dill salad
1 boiled egg
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 dessert spoon sumac
Drain the beans.
Slice the onion thinly and rub with sumac and salt.
Chop the tomato and dill.
Make a dressing with olive oil and lemon and mix the ingredients.
Top with the sliced egg.
Rubbing the onion with sumac softens its sharpness.
Couscous and corn salad
1 cup boiling water
1 cup boiled corn
1 red pepper, 1 cucumber (diced)
Put the couscous in a bowl, add salt and 1 tablespoon of olive oil, pour over the boiling water; cover and leave for 5 minutes.
Fluff the grains with a fork and let cool.
Cut the vegetables into small cubes and finely chop the herbs.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and cumin.
Mix everything and chill in the fridge for 15 minutes.
If the dressing is added while the couscous is hot it turns mushy; wait for it to cool.
Red cabbage and apple salad
Half a small red cabbage
1 green apple
Shred the cabbage very finely, rub with salt, leave for 10 minutes and squeeze out the liquid.
Cut the apple and carrot into julienne strips.
Whisk the yogurt, olive oil and lemon.
Toss everything together.
Garnish with walnuts.
Rubbing with salt softens the cabbage.
Broccoli and walnut salad
1 broccoli
Separate the broccoli into small florets, boil for 3 minutes and plunge into cold water.
Finely chop the onion.
Make a dressing with yogurt, olive oil, lemon and salt.
Mix the broccoli, raisins and onion with the dressing.
Add the walnuts and serve.
Plunging it into cold water keeps the broccoli’s colour.
Buckwheat pilaf with mushrooms
1.5 cups buckwheat
2.5 cups hot water
Sauté the onion and sliced mushrooms in oil for 8 minutes until the liquid evaporates.
Add the buckwheat and toast for 2 minutes.
Add the hot water and salt and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add the butter and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Buckwheat is gluten-free.
Serve hot alongside the main dish.
Brown rice pilaf with chickpeas
1.5 cups brown rice
3 cups hot water
Soak the brown rice in lukewarm water for 1 hour and drain.
Toast the rice in butter for 3 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, hot water and salt.
Once boiling, cook covered over low heat for 35 minutes.
Let rest for 10 minutes.
Brown rice takes longer than white; soaking shortens the time.
